decisions.statement: The properties judged are the properties a page type has after shadowing.
An inherited key and a declared key meet as surely as two declared keys.
Two declarations at the same key naming different properties collide.
No narrowing makes those two declarations one.
A restatement has the property's own key.
A narrowing stands where another declaration already stands.
A restatement narrows.
Required never loosens.
A max only falls.
A unique kind only narrows.
A unique kind goes from `page` to `page-type` to `page-property`.
A unique kind never goes back.
A restatement letting a unique kind go altogether widens that kind.
Whether a property is carried once or many times never changes.
A record property's fields are each held to one key like a page type's.
A record property takes no declaration from any other page.
The declarers of a property are read from the index rather than composed here.
A page type is judged when the change has that page type or a property that type declares.
A page type under a judged page type is judged as well.
A record property is judged on the same two counts.
A declaration reaching no page property is not judged here.
A name reaching nothing is `relation-resolves`'s to refuse.
Nothing here judges a key's format nor whether any page type declares the property.

definition: the check with each of a declarer's keys to one property, narrowed where restated
